2007 Chevy Impala

P0455 Evaporative Emission (EVAP):

System Large Leak Detect (Symptom 00) - Test Failed Since DTC Clear, Test No Passed Since Power Up -

P0521 Engine Oil Pressure (EOP):

Sensor Performance (Symptom 00) - Test Failed Since DTC Clear. -

P1174 Fuel Trim Cylinder Balance:

(Symptom 00) - Test Failed Since DTC Clear, History DTC. -

P2122 Accelerator Pedal Position (APP):

Sensor 1 Circuit Low Voltage (Symptom 00) - Test Failed Since DTC Clear, History DTC, Warning Indicator Requested. -

first one is either a charcoal canister hose undone or most likely you need a new gas cap. 2nd one is your oil pressure switch here is the part. I believe that's the 3.8l. if I remember correctly that sensor is screwed in right above the oil filter. careful with your electrical plug.

the p1174 is a tricky one. could be caused by a lot of things. fix your other issues then circle back to that one may be related. never hurts to run some sea foam through her.

p2122 accelerator pedal position. newer cars have a "fly by wire" type of setup which is a potentiometer embedded in your throttle. sometimes they just fail. but it never hurts to find the connector for your foot pedal should be within six inches or so of the pedal, maybe folded behind the carpet or something. disconnect that plug and run some electronic cleaner over the plug and apply some dielectric grease. try to clean up where the pedal actuates and spray some cleaner in that joint to try to get some in contact with the potentiometer in the pedal. most likely youll have to replace. double check the procedure on youtube or goole to see if there is a component learning procedure (program the cars computer to the new part. usually takes a sequence of actions like key turning, throttle pressing, etc with the key in the acc. position. may not have anything and be plug and play though.

youll have to clear all codes and see which ones come back. good luck!
